title: Operator sees the exact issue text and what was stripped before consenting
asA: operator being asked to submit findings
iWant: rcf feedback preview to print the exact rendered issue title and body, the destination repo and its visibility, and a redaction ledger that lists every rule-triggered replacement so I can see what was stripped
soThat: my yes is informed and nothing surprising leaves the machine

acceptanceCriteria.description: rcf feedback preview renders each pending entry as the title and body that would be filed on GitHub (using src/feedback/render.js templates from section 4.3 of the design), lists the destination repo and its declared visibility (public, private, or unresolved), and prints the redaction ledger as diff-style lines ("- before  + after") with the rule name. --json emits the same as a machine-readable object per entry. No network calls. The kv-secret rule (design section 5 rule 5) is driven by the shared SECRET_KEY_VOCABULARY constant exported from src/feedback/redact.js (design amendment R3a) so the first-pass redactor, the residual safeguard pass and the rule-9 URL-credential scanner cover exactly the same open vocabulary of key stems (secret, token, password, passwd, passphrase, pw, pwd, pass, key, apikey/api_key/api-key, privatekey/private_key/private-key, accesskey/access_key/access-key, clientsecret/client_secret/client-secret, bearer, credential/credentials/cred/creds, session, cookie, signature, sig, salt; hash carries a 16+-value length guard); the match is right-bounded at a word edge so `keyword` and `authors` do not fold but `dbpassword` still does. Design amendment R4 (round 5) extends the rule-5 pass so a vocabulary key labelling a value-shape token of 8+ chars with any separator (markdown table pipes, whitespace runs, tabs, hyphens, arrows, HTML numeric entities, or the prose bridges is / was / set to) also folds, with a mixed-classes gate on the value that keeps ordinary prose (`the password is required`, `the password field is required`) intact.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture project with one entry whose body contains an absolute path, an email, a non-allowlisted hostname, a token-shaped string, a private IPv4 (10.0.5.7), an em-dash, an oversize body block, an operator name that matches a seeded rcf/.identity/profile.md ## Name line, AND at least one shortname-key secret (`pw=`), one URL-embedded credential (a Slack webhook path), one markdown-table row with a vocabulary key and a mixed-class value (`| password | Sup3rSecretV@lue!! |`) and one prose bridge (`the password Sup3rSecretV@lue1234 is bad`)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator runs rcf feedback preview --json
acceptanceCriteria.then: the JSON output carries titleRendered, bodyRendered, destination { repo, visibility }, and ledger[] entries whose rule names include project-root, absolute-path, email, hostname, secret-token, private-ip, operator-identity, size-shape and url-credential; the rendered body contains none of the original secret substrings (including the shortname-key value, the webhook path segment, the markdown-table value and the prose-bridge value), none of the private IP, none of the operator-name tokens, no em-dash, and is at most 8 KB

acceptanceCriteria.description: When a body still matches a rule-5 secret pattern on the second redaction pass, preview marks the entry as "residual secret at line N" and submit refuses that entry. Other pending entries are unaffected. The exact refusing line is shown to the operator so the agent can rewrite the body.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture project with two entries, one containing a token that survives the first pass through obfuscation and one clean
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator runs rcf feedback preview then rcf feedback submit --yes
acceptanceCriteria.then: the tainted entry is shown with the residual-secret line; submit does not send the tainted entry; the clean entry is submitted (or fallbacks to bundle if that path applies); exit code is 3 while any residual-secret entry is still pending

acceptanceCriteria.description: The stored entries.jsonl body is never mutated by preview. A byte-for-byte comparison of entries.jsonl before and after preview is identical; the redaction lives only in the rendered output.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture project with entries whose bodies contain redactable content
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator runs rcf feedback preview repeatedly
acceptanceCriteria.then: a sha-256 of entries.jsonl before and after each preview run matches

acceptanceCriteria.description: After rendering and normalising the fully assembled issue body (and, for the bundle path, each bundle file), a final whole-text residual-secret pass runs findResidualSecrets over the whole text with multiline patterns. Any hit means the entry stays pending (preview marks it refused-residual and submit refuses that entry with exit 3) and no create/comment/bundle-write occurs for it. The safeguard is defence-in-depth: it catches multiline shapes (e.g. an em-dash-delimited PEM block that survives per-field redaction of a slice-2-style body) that a per-line scan could not see. The safeguard shares the SECRET_KEY_VOCABULARY constant with the first-pass redactor and the rule-9 URL-credential scanner (design amendment R3a), so a shortname-key value (`pw=...`, `pwd=...`) or a webhook-path shape (`/services/<token>`, `/api/webhooks/<token>`, `/bot<token>/method`) that reappears after per-field normalisation is caught by the same set the first pass used.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture project with an entry whose body assembles into a rendered issue body containing a shape a per-line residual scan would miss (a multiline PEM block or a token buried inside a longer identifier)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator runs rcf feedback preview then rcf feedback submit --yes
acceptanceCriteria.then: preview surfaces the residual line and the tainted entry stays pending; submit exits 3 without a create/comment for that entry and without writing a bundle whose text carries the residual shape

acceptanceCriteria.description: The operator-identity substitution (design section 5 rule 6) applies word-boundary and stopword guards so a common noun that happens to appear in the operator's identity name is not folded. A RESERVED_IDENTITY_TOKENS constant, exported from src/feedback/redact.js and defence-in-depth applied at every operator-name token loop, blocks the fold when the whitespace-separated token (case-insensitive) is one of: agent, agents, user, users, operator, operators, admin, admins, root, client, clients, server, servers, service, services, system, systems, name, main, test, code, api, apis, anon, anonymous, human, humans, dev, ops, sre, docs, developer, developers, engineer, engineers, team, teams. Substitution still fires for a real given name (Alice, Smith) even when the full identity string contains a stopword. The URL and prose canon phrase 'the agent files feedback' survives unmodified when the identity contains 'agent'. Rationale: the rcf-lite ecosystem uses 'agent' as a canonical noun (RULE 17, docs paths); operator-identity folds must be driven by real identity values, never by a bare common noun.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture project whose rcf/.identity/profile.md ## Name reads 'The Agent Alice', and a body containing the docs URL 'https://stravica.ai/docs/rcf/how-the-agent-files-feedback', the prose 'when the agent stops the queue', and the personal name 'Alice reviewed this'
acceptanceCriteria.when: the redactor runs over the body with the seeded operator identity
acceptanceCriteria.then: the docs URL survives verbatim; the prose 'when the agent stops the queue' survives verbatim; the personal name 'Alice' folds to <operator>; the ledger records an operator-identity row for 'Alice' but no row for 'agent' or 'the'

acceptanceCriteria.description: The rule-4 bare-hostname redactor treats filename tokens carrying a known file extension as NOT hostnames. A candidate hostname match whose trailing dot-label is in a bundled FILE_EXTENSIONS set (initially md, mdx, json, yml, yaml, txt, js, mjs, cjs, ts, tsx, html, css, png, svg, sh, csv, log, lock) is left intact and no ledger row is written for it (design amendment R5d). The negative lookbehind on the hostname regex additionally excludes '-' so that filename fragments embedded in a larger identifier (`Backstory-product-brief.md`) cannot start a match after a hyphen. The extension shortlist is merged at call time from an `extensions` array on src/feedback/redact-allowlist.json alongside the existing `hosts` field, so operators can extend it the same way they extend hosts. Design amendment R5e (added 0.28.3 per HQ 2026-09-22 ruling on Codex P1-5 deferred from PR #242): candidate hostnames whose trailing dot-label is a single letter are also treated as filename fragments, not hostnames. Rationale: single-letter TLDs are not registrable domains in normal prose and folding them yields more false positives (short identifiers, abbreviated references) than legitimate hostname redactions. Design amendment R5f (added 0.28.3, #243): the rule-3 email regex is bounded so it does not consume the git protocol sentinel `git@<host>` inside a URL whose scheme is `git+ssh://`, `ssh://` or `git://`, nor the bare git-remote shape `git@<host>:<owner>/<repo>` (colon followed by a non-space path). Rationale: `git@<host>` is a URI userinfo construct, not an email; folding it destroys evidence pointers copied from git remotes and clone URLs. Real email addresses in surrounding prose still fold. Design amendment R5g (added 0.28.3, #246): when the operator identity Name (rcf/.identity/profile.md ## Name) is empty, whitespace only, or contains only reserved-noun tokens (RESERVED_IDENTITY_TOKENS from AC-15601-5), buildRedactionContext emits a one-line visible warning to stderr naming the file and stating that identity folding is disabled. The warning is emitted once per redaction context build. Folding still skips (per AC-15601-5) but the operator is no longer left thinking their identity is in force.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture project with a body containing the tokens 'Backstory-product-brief.md', 'intake.json', 'report.log', 'foo.example.com', 'foo.example.com/path', 'Backstory-example.com', 'a.b.c', the URL 'git+ssh://git@github.com/owner/repo.git#v1.0.0', the URL 'ssh://git@example.internal/owner/repo.git', the bare git remote 'git@github.com:owner/repo.git', and a prose email 'alice@example.com'; and a rcf/.identity/profile.md whose ## Name line is either absent, whitespace only, or reads 'The Agent Operator' (stopword-only)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the redactor runs over the body with the default allowlist
acceptanceCriteria.then: 'Backstory-product-brief.md', 'intake.json' and 'report.log' survive verbatim with no ledger row for a hostname substitution on their basename; 'foo.example.com' folds to <host> via rule 4; 'foo.example.com/path' folds via rule 4 bare-host (the URL rule requires a scheme; the token here has none); 'Backstory-example.com' folds to '<host>' (the trailing label is not in the extension set); 'a.b.c' survives verbatim with no hostname ledger row (single-letter trailing label per R5e); 'git+ssh://git@github.com/owner/repo.git#v1.0.0' survives verbatim - the `git@` sentinel is NOT rewritten by the email rule (R5f) and github.com is on the allowlist; 'ssh://git@example.internal/owner/repo.git' has the `git@` sentinel preserved (R5f stash) and the host `example.internal` folded to '<host>' by the extended URL rule 4 which now matches ssh/git+ssh/git schemes with optional userinfo; 'git@github.com:owner/repo.git' has the `git@` sentinel preserved (R5f) and github.com is on the allowlist so it survives verbatim; 'alice@example.com' in surrounding prose still folds to '<email>' (rule 3 email); and when the identity Name is empty/whitespace/stopword-only, stderr carries exactly one visible warning line naming rcf/.identity/profile.md and stating that identity folding is disabled. Extending the allowlist with `extensions: ["xyz"]` in redact-allowlist.json (or the operator overlay) makes 'file.xyz' also survive.
